title: Acclimation dynamics of cyanobacteria to low UV-B radiation
content: UV-B (218 to 315 nm) radiation accounts for about 5% of total UV radiation. It has a severe impact on both terrestrial and aquatic creatures. UV-B can affect cellular processes by damaging biomolecules and generating reactive oxygen species (Jenkin 2009). However, its effect depends on several factors, including intensity, duration of exposure, species, and other environmental conditions (Häder et al. 2015). Although exposure to UV-B radiation has an adverse impact on various photosynthetic organisms, a few studies have reported that low levels of UV-B can have a positive effect on these organisms (Wargent et al. 2015).
